questions.q: What is the real skill this lesson teaches, underneath the Hartwell example?
options: Writing KQL joins
Requirements clarification — turning a vague security ask into a specific, scoped deliverable
Configuring Windows Firewall profiles
Choosing which Sentinel pricing tier to buy
questions.explain: This lesson is entirely about turning "tighten things up and let me know if something gets through" into a specific, written project scope before any server is touched.

questions.q: Why does the phishing near-miss point specifically at "failed sign-ins followed by a success" as the first detection rule's target?
options: Because it's the only pattern Microsoft Sentinel supports out of the box
Because that's the pattern a phished credential would most likely produce if an attacker tried to use it
Because Windows Event Viewer only logs that one event type
Because it requires no KQL to detect
questions.explain: An attacker using a stolen credential typically guesses a few times before, or instead of, succeeding — so a failure cluster followed by a success is the realistic signature of that exact scenario.

questions.q: Which four servers does Mara scope this project to?
options: Every server Hartwell operates, across all departments
Two Windows servers (HRU-FILE01, HRU-APP01) and two Linux servers (hru-web01, hru-db01)
Only the public-facing outage-reporting portal
Four Windows domain controllers
questions.explain: The scope is a representative handful covering both operating systems and both an internal-only system and an internet-facing one, not the entire environment.

questions.q: Which of these is explicitly OUT of scope for this Beginner project?
options: Hardening the four named servers to a documented baseline
A full penetration test and vulnerability scan of Hartwell's entire network
Building one Sentinel analytics rule for the chosen detection target
Producing a written checklist Dale's team can reuse
questions.explain: A full pentest/vulnerability scan is real, valuable work, but it's a different project with different tools — not part of this scoped engagement.

questions.q: What makes the written requirement in this lesson "specific enough"?
options: It lists every setting in the CIS Benchmarks
It names the exact servers, the baseline standard to apply, the detection pattern, and the deliverable
It avoids naming Dale Granger directly
It is written entirely in KQL
questions.explain: A specific requirement names scope, baseline, detection target, and deliverable — the same test used in this course's other capstones: a teammate given only that sentence would build the same thing.
